summary.intent: Run the full E2E test suite against recent code changes (SDK extraction refactor) and diagnose any failures.
summary.outcome: Identified and fixed a broken import in E2E tests caused by vault functions moving from @cipherbox/crypto to @cipherbox/core during the SDK extraction refactor. Committed the fix. 7 remaining test failures were determined to be pre-existing infrastructure issues, not regressions from this branch.

repo: The SDK extraction refactor moved initializeVault, encryptVaultKeys, and decryptVaultKeys from @cipherbox/crypto to @cipherbox/core, but E2E tests were not updated to reflect this.
The E2E test .env defaults to the staging API (https://api-staging.cipherbox.cc), not localhost, which causes auth mismatches when running locally.
14 E2E tests pass (MFA flows + wallet login); 7 tests fail at login — either KEY_UNWRAPPING_FAILED with local API (stale vault data) or redirect loop with staging API.
Phase 19 (someguy sidecar) is a suspected root cause of E2E test failures; Phase 18 (instrumentation only) was the last known good state.
The web3auth-based auth path is considered flaky in E2E environments; migrating to EVM wallet-based auth is being considered as it requires no special config.

code.finding: Imported decryptVaultKeys (and likely initializeVault, encryptVaultKeys) from @cipherbox/crypto — must now import vault functions from @cipherbox/core, crypto utilities (hexToBytes, bytesToHex, deriveIpnsName) remain in @cipherbox/crypto.
Was missing @cipherbox/core as a dependency; added to support the corrected imports.
decryptVaultKeys implementation in @cipherbox/core is identical to the original in @cipherbox/crypto — the move was a relocation, not a reimplementation.

workflow: When E2E tests fail with a SyntaxError on import, check if a refactor moved exports between packages before investigating test logic.
Stashing changes and running tests on original code is a useful regression check, but only works if the original code can actually run the tests.
GH Actions E2E run history is the reference for pinpointing when tests started breaking across phases.

friction: The E2E test .env pointed to staging by default, making it ambiguous whether failures were environment mismatches or real regressions.
Local API had stale vault test data, causing KEY_UNWRAPPING_FAILED that looked like a code regression but was an infrastructure issue.
Because the import error blocked all tests from running on the original branch, no direct before/after regression comparison was possible.
Web3Auth-based E2E login is fragile across environments (local vs staging), requiring workarounds that add noise to failure analysis.
open_items: Investigate GH Actions E2E run history to pinpoint whether Phase 19 (someguy sidecar) introduced the 7 login-path test failures.
Consider migrating all E2E tests from web3auth-based auth to EVM wallet-based authentication to eliminate environment-specific auth flakiness.
Resolve the local E2E test infrastructure issue: local vault test data is stale/mismatched with the test-login endpoint keypair.
Confirm whether the 7 failing tests were already broken before this branch or if Phase 19 is the true culprit.
